agree.reason: The pilot pace and the 15-a-week target make a strong case, but the two members from advertising will see that the memo never covers the first-year cash gap, when ad money stops in January and membership is still building.

honest.reason: The memo makes replacement a target rather than a promise and marks the retention figure as a gap to fill, but it says the 36% drop happened 'over two years' when it happened in one year, so a core fact is wrong.

works_the_facts.reason: The derived figures are good (about $20k a year from the pilot, 875 members to break even, 1,000 as the target, 15 a week against the pilot's roughly 35), but the decline is presented as slower than it was, which weakens the strongest argument.

right_comparison.reason: Treating ads as a falling source rather than a fixed $84k is the right comparison, but the memo spreads the 36% drop over two years and so projects $65–70k, when the one-year rate points to about $54k next year.

qualification.reason: The safeguard can be checked: monthly reports, a midpoint of 500 members at six months, and named fallback options if that number is missed.

objections.reason: The memo deals with the long-serving salesperson and the concern that loyal readers signed up first, but it says nothing about the first-year revenue gap or why ads can't run alongside membership, which is what sales-minded members will ask.

fit.reason: It is a clear memo that fits on about one page, with the decision stated at the top, though the placeholders still need filling in.
